articles.title: Financial security in childhood predicts a later loss of religious faith
articles.summary: Young people who grow up in financially secure households are slightly more likely to lose their belief in God by the time they reach adulthood, suggesting modern material comfort may reduce the psychological need for religious support systems.

articles.title: What if the brain does not create consciousness?
articles.summary: Christof Koch is taking on one of science’s deepest mysteries: how the brain creates conscious experience, or whether it creates it at all. He argues that materialism has yet to solve this “hard problem” and will explore puzzling phenomena such as near-death experiences and terminal lucidity. His work points toward the possibility that consciousness may be woven into reality itself.

articles.title: Scientists are using biological markers to take the guesswork out of depression treatment
articles.summary: Researchers have developed a predictive algorithm using brain connectivity and behavioral tests to forecast antidepressant outcomes. A recent study suggests this tool can identify depressed patients who are highly likely to benefit from standard medications.

articles.title: Researchers find evidence connecting a specific blood protein to brain tissue loss
articles.summary: High levels of a specific blood protein during midlife suggest an increased risk for vascular dementia. Researchers found evidence that this protein might alter immune activity and contribute to the gradual loss of healthy brain tissue.

articles.title: Even More Deception: Objective Misalignment in Mixed-Motive LLM Multi-Agent Systems
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.26120v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs)-powered multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed in mixed-motive environments, where agents operate under asymmetric information and strategic deception due to conflicting or hidden objectives. In these settings, misalignment with collective goals becomes a central concern. We propose a novel framework for evaluating objective misalignment using the social deduction game Werewolf, modifying the objective of a single agent while preserving its assigned role. Across LLMs from four different model families and sizes

articles.title: ClinLens: Towards Long-Horizon Coding Agents for Longitudinal Multimodal Clinical Data Science
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.26155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clinical data-science agents must transform heterogeneous longitudinal records into auditable analyses, yet existing benchmarks largely isolate medical question answering, structured-table reasoning, or generic scientific repositories. We introduce CLINLENS, a benchmark of 200 executable tasks over five linked MIMIC resources spanning structured electronic health records, notes, electrocardiograms, chest radiographs, and echocardiograms. A 4 x 5 taxonomy crosses four patient-time scopes with five analysis capabilities. Program-first reverse synth

articles.title: When benchmark inferences do not compose: Projectibility in AI evaluation
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.26159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An AI benchmark result rarely reaches a consequential claim in one step. Evaluators generalize it to further cases, interpret it as evidence of capability, extrapolate it to new tasks, transport it to another system or site, and combine it with assumptions about human review and downstream consequences. Validity-centred approaches require evidence for each claim. This paper identifies a further epistemic problem: warranted links don't automatically make a warranted chain. articles.title: Your gut may help your brain decide what to remember
articles.summary: Signals traveling from the gut to the brain may help turn meals into lasting memories. Rats showed stronger memory activity after consuming nutritious foods, but not after drinking sweet liquids with little or no nutritional value. Blocking the vagus nerve erased this effect and made it harder for the animals to remember where food had been located. Over time, diets high in fat and sugar also weakened this memory system.

articles.title: Eating within 8 hours may help keep the aging brain sharp
articles.summary: Eating within a shorter daily window may help protect certain thinking skills as people age. In a small six-month trial, older women who limited eating to about 8 to 9 hours a day performed better on planning and problem-solving tests than those who ate over 12 hours. Both groups lost similar amounts of weight, hinting that when people eat could matter in addition to how much they eat.

articles.title: A hidden Alzheimer’s tipping point may decide who gets dementia
articles.summary: Scientists have identified a possible tipping point that helps determine whether Alzheimer’s-related brain changes lead to dementia. The key may lie in how the brain’s immune cells respond to plaques and tau, offering a promising new target for treatments designed to extend cognitive resilience.

articles.title: Psilocybin-assisted therapy shows promise for veterans with severe, treatment-resistant PTSD
articles.summary: A pilot clinical trial suggests that psilocybin combined with psychotherapy is safe and well-tolerated by veterans with severe, treatment-resistant PTSD. The study found that most participants no longer met the diagnostic criteria for PTSD.

articles.title: New space station study reveals a hidden side effect of long-term microgravity on the human brain
articles.summary: Astronauts are notoriously slow and deliberate when moving in space. But a new study from the China Space Station reveals it’s not just about safety—microgravity actually tricks the human brain into underestimating its own body mass.

articles.title: Long COVID symptoms linked to measurable damage in the brain’s dopamine system
articles.summary: A recent study provides evidence that people experiencing long COVID show a measurable reduction in the brain’s dopamine-releasing neurons. These physical changes tend to be associated with persistent symptoms like apathy, memory problems, and slowed physical movements.
